action: If SCTP is not needed, block the module from loading (a modprobe.d rule such as 'install sctp /bin/false'), and watch your distribution's kernel updates; Xint says a kernel patch is expected in the coming weeks.
exec: An unpatched Linux kernel flaw lets an attacker who already runs code on a server, including inside a container, become root on the host.
plain: Researchers say they found an unpatched flaw in the Linux kernel's SCTP networking code that can turn a foothold on a server into full control, and a fix has not been released yet.

key_findings: Xint describes a use-after-free or double free in the SCTP send path, introduced in Linux v4.15 in 2018, reachable when an association is moved to another socket while a send is waiting.
Chained with one of its five nginx flaws, it gave root on the host, including from a Docker container; Xint withholds most exploit details until a kernel patch exists.
No CVE number or kernel patch is stated; Xint says the patch will come in the coming weeks (nginx2root.com).
A post on oss-security (Rich Felker, 18 November) advises anyone not needing SCTP to block the module.
recommendations: Block the sctp module where not needed.

sources.name: Xint: NGINX2Root, section 6 (Linux kernel SCTP flaw)
oss-security: Another (?) Linux kernel SCTP vuln undisclosed

summary: Xint (Theori) says a separate, still-unpatched Linux kernel flaw in the SCTP subsystem, found alongside five nginx vulnerabilities, lets a local attacker gain root, including escaping a Docker container. The bug has existed since Linux 4.15 (2018). Xint withholds exploit details and says a patch is due in the coming weeks. No CVE or exploitation in the wild is stated.
title: Xint discloses unpatched Linux kernel SCTP privilege-escalation flaw chained with nginx bugs

validation.note: Xint's own write-up read in full; the oss-security thread only repeats Xint's site and points to the same blog. No kernel maintainer or CVE record found, so the flaw is reported by one party.

review.note: Compared Nov 18 date, unpatched SCTP LPE, no CVE, patch in coming weeks, modprobe block advice against Xint post (partly read) and oss-security post by Rich Felker
